dimension: DIMENSION 2 — In-repo parallelism assets and the deterministic-parallel design for gum-core
findings: fs-exec is UNBUILDABLE in this checkout — verified, not just read: crates/fs-exec/Cargo.toml line 14 declares `asupersync = { path = "../../../asupersync" }`, /home/user/asupersync does not exist, and `cargo check -p fs-exec` fails at MANIFEST LOAD ("failed to read /home/user/asupersync/Cargo.toml"). Consequence: gum-core cannot use fs-exec (TilePool, Cx/Budget/CancelGate, RunId, the reduce module) in this checkout, and any transitive dep on fs-exec poisons the whole build. The repo already knows this: ROADMAP_v3.md lines 99-104 records the recurrent portability note (B3 vendored jacobi_eigh, B2 wrote an internal FFT), and Phase F3 fixed fs-la/fs-fft with a default-ON `exec` cargo feature (crates/fs-la/Cargo.toml lines 22-27: `exec = ["dep:fs-exec"]`) — so gum-core CAN dep on fs-la with `default-features = false`, but gets only the serial non-pooled paths that way.

fs-exec/src/reduce.rs is nevertheless THE design template and is internally dependency-free (uses only crate::kernel::Reduce trait + std): pairwise_fold with the SHAPE RULE 'split at the largest power of two strictly below n' (a pure function of item count, never of scheduling/arrival/thread count), Neumaier `Compensated` partials whose merge is a two-sum (Reduce-composable so compensated global sums ride the same fixed tree), BLOCK=256 per-block accumulation in det_sum/det_dot (BLOCK is part of the bit contract), det_dot forms products UNFUSED so FMA targets agree, det_argmin/argmax tie-break to LOWEST index, det_min/max under IEEE total_cmp, and audit_accumulator (seeded-permutation arrival-order audit with smallest-prefix localization). ~200 LOC, vendorable verbatim into gum-core (the B3 jacobi_eigh precedent with a documented swap-back), or better: split fs-exec's reduce.rs into a dep-free fs-reduce crate upstream — exactly the Phase-F upstreaming pattern already executed for fs-la.

fs-simd IS buildable from gum-core: its full dependency closure is std-only (fs-simd -> fs-substrate -> fs-obs -> nothing external; verified in all three Cargo.tomls). It offers a resolved-ONCE function table (`ops()`, OnceLock, no per-call branching) with a two-class determinism contract: ELEMENTWISE fused ops (axpy, scale, mul_elem, fma3, fmacc) are BITWISE-identical across tiers (scalar twin uses mul_add; capsules gated by a tier-equivalence battery over lens 0..67 incl. NaN payload/inf/signed-zero cases), while REDUCTIONS (dot, sum) have a fixed per-tier shape but only an envelope guarantee ACROSS tiers (documented as machine identity, never run jitter). Usability for gum-core: the ANF stepper's flat 4N^3-vector updates are exactly axpy shapes (v -= (dt/h^3)g, q += dt*v — anf.rs lines 159-172) and can use ops().axpy bitwise-safely; the sector/stencil inner loops operate on [f64;4] / [[f64;4];3] register-local quaternion blocks where LLVM already autovectorizes and fs-simd's slice primitives don't fit — leave them scalar-source. HARD RULE: golden-bearing reductions must NEVER use ops().dot/sum (cross-ISA bits differ); use the fixed pairwise/Neumaier tree instead.

fs-alloc is std-only (zero deps — verified) and directly usable: ALLOC_ALIGN=128 unconditional (superset of Apple 128 B / x86-64 64 B cache lines), `CachePadded<T>` (#[repr(align(128))]) for the per-tile partial-sum slots so 4 workers never false-share, ArenaPool scope arenas with O(1) cancel reclaim for per-iteration gradient/scratch buffers, ShardedPool for recurring same-shape per-thread scratch (the a_pack pattern).

fs-la gemm.rs codifies the repo's tiling + threading grain (the pattern to copy, even though the pooled path is exec-gated): (a) an explicit bit contract split — KC=256 is PART of the bit contract ('changing it legitimately changes bits -> golden bump with justification'), MC=128/NC=512 are bit-neutral pure m/n tiling, with a GEMM_BIT_SEMANTICS_VERSION constant pinned by golden-couplings.json and `xtask check-goldens`; (b) the parallel engine gemm_f64_parallel_with (lines 518-600, NO fs-exec needed — plain std::thread::scope) packs B once per (jc,pc) chunk, shares it read-only, and dispenses disjoint MC-row C bands from a Mutex<chunks_mut enumerate> dispenser — 'a band's content is a pure function of the band, never of which thread computed it or in what order; the lock guards ASSIGNMENT only', so the parallel path is BITWISE-FREE (no golden bump), gated across thread counts; (c) hard-won scheduling facts encoded in comments: workers = t.min(bands) because excess spawns measured 2-9x slower on the 64-thread ts1 box, and the work-stealing dispenser exists because equal static shares let heterogeneous E-cores drag the chunk (measured on M4 Pro). Repo grain: ZERO external runtime deps anywhere in the workspace; parallelism is std::thread::scope + Mutex/atomic dispensers; rayon appears nowhere.

gum-core current hot-loop census (what must be parallelized): (1) fs-gum-field sector.rs measure() — 'straight sequential f64 sums in fixed ascending (i,j,k) order' into a single Accum (its own module docs pin this order); (2) fs-gum-statics engine.rs eval() pass 1 — four scalar accumulators (s_e2/s_e4/s_det/s_det2) via for_each_point, same flat order; (3) eval() pass 2 gradient — a SCATTER: each eval point computes flux P[3][4] + gq[4] (point_flux) and scatters +-1/+-2 stencil-adjoint contributions into up to 12 neighbor cells of g (Central4, lines 373-420) or 8 cells per corner (Corner, lines 428-457) — races under naive tiling AND per-cell arrival order is the loop order, so this is the one pass that needs restructuring; (4) anf.rs stepper — flat axpy updates, per-cell renormalize and tangent projections: all disjoint-write, embarrassingly parallel; (5) g.norm() — a fixed sequential sum. The ghost rind is FIXED VACUUM (2 layers, Field3 padded p=n+4): there is no ghost EXCHANGE at all in the current physics — tiles only need read-only access to 2 planes beyond their slab, which shared &Field3 gives for free on shared memory; the rind becomes a real halo exchange only at the GPU/distributed stage.

PROTOTYPE VALIDATED on this box (scratchpad gumbench/src/bin/tiledet.rs): N=96 grid, i-slab tiles of 4 planes (24 tiles, pure function of N), per-tile serial (i,j,k)-ascending accumulation, fixed largest-pow2-below pairwise combine; serial-tiled vs 4-thread (std::thread::scope + atomic tile dispenser + per-tile slots, combine after join) is bit_identical=true BY CONSTRUCTION; the CURRENT flat sequential order gives a DIFFERENT last-bits result (9.83072230548363030e7 tiled vs 9.83072230548577905e7 flat — divergence at the 12th significant digit), confirming a one-time golden re-freeze is required; measured speedup 1.99-2.43x on the 4 container cores.
design_recommendation: Deterministic-parallel gum-core kernel layer (new dep-free crate, e.g. fs-gum-kern, path-dep'd by fs-gum-field/statics; vendors fs-exec's pairwise_fold+Compensated ~200 LOC with a documented swap-back to a future dep-free fs-reduce split — the B3/F3 precedent). (1) CANONICAL TILED ORDER: decompose the N^3 grid into i-slabs of fixed thickness TILE_I=4 planes (i-slabs are the SoA-contiguous axis in aidx layout; tile count = ceil(N/4) is a pure function of N, NEVER of thread count — TILE_I joins the bit contract exactly like fs-la's KC, with a GUM_BIT_SEMANTICS_VERSION constant and golden-couplings pin). The SERIAL path computes per-tile partials in tile order and combines them up the largest-pow2-below pairwise tree; the THREADED path computes the SAME per-tile partials (identical per-tile arithmetic, ascending (i,j,k) within tile) into CachePadded per-tile slots via std::thread::scope with an atomic/Mutex tile dispenser (fs-la's band-dispenser pattern, workers = threads.min(tiles)), joins, then runs the IDENTICAL tree. Serial vs 4-thread is bit-identical by construction — scheduling and steal order are provably irrelevant because every rounding decision is a function of (N, TILE_I) alone. This costs ONE deliberate golden bump (tiled order != current flat order, divergence measured at the 12th digit); re-freeze with justification per the gemm KC-contract precedent — the v2 tolerance-band fallback is NOT needed, this stays in the bit-identical class. Use plain per-tile f64 accumulation to match current physics semantics; offer Compensated variants where the physics wants them. (2) GRADIENT — convert the pass-2 scatter into two gather passes: pass A (embarrassingly parallel, disjoint writes) evaluates point_flux per eval point and STORES P[3][4]+gq[4] into a 16*N^3 f64 buffer (128 B/cell, 113 MB at N=96 — fine; slab-staged variant needed by N=192); pass B (embarrassingly parallel, disjoint writes) has each OUTPUT cell gather its 12 (Central4) or 8-corner contributions from the stored buffer in a PINNED fixed order (axis x,y,z; +-1 before +-2; then gq; order documented as bit contract). No atomics, no races, and the two passes map 1:1 onto two GPU kernels later — this is the CPU/GPU-portable shape. Gate the rewrite with the existing FD-vs-analytic gradient gate (1.2e-6) plus a gather-vs-scatter relative-agreement gate (~1e-13; they are legitimately not bitwise-equal) before freezing new goldens. (3) ANF STEPPER: per-cell velocity/position updates, renormalize, and tangent projections parallelize over the same tile decomposition with disjoint writes (bit-identical trivially, no reduction); ghost rind is fixed vacuum so there is NO exchange — the per-iteration structure is [update tiles] -> barrier -> [eval pass1 tiled reduction] -> [pass A] -> barrier -> [pass B] -> [gnorm via fixed-tree det_dot] -> serial arrest/accept logic (the dt controller stays serial and identical). Keep ONE std::thread::scope per eval (5 barriers/iter is noise: eval is 285 ms at N=96 vs ~10 us scope overhead). (4) THREADS: std::thread::scope, NO rayon — the workspace has zero external runtime deps, fs-la's parallel GEMM and fs-exec's pool are both hand-rolled scoped-thread designs, gum-core crates are declared std-only closures, and determinism-by-slots makes rayon's scheduler buy nothing but a dependency against the repo grain. (5) fs-simd: adopt ops().axpy/fmacc for the flat 4N^3 ANF vector ops (bitwise across tiers), never ops().dot/sum for goldens; leave [f64;4] stencil micro-math to LLVM.

risks: One-time golden bump is unavoidable: the tiled canonical order provably differs from the current flat sequential order (measured, 12th significant digit at N=96). Every sector/gradient/e2e golden (six Merkle roots, ~200 claims) downstream of a reduction must be deliberately re-frozen with justification in the same change that introduces the contract — the gemm KC / GEMM_BIT_SEMANTICS_VERSION precedent; doing it piecemeal would strand goldens.

The scatter-to-gather gradient rewrite is the largest correctness risk (adjoint stencil sign/offset errors at the 0/1/2-cell boundary rows where the current code drops ghost flux). Mitigation exists in-repo: the FD-vs-analytic gradient gate (1.2e-6) plus a temporary gather-vs-scatter agreement gate (~1e-13 relative — they are NOT bitwise-equal, per-cell addition order changes).

TILE_I and the pass-B gather order become PART of the bit contract (like KC): any later retuning of tile thickness for cache or GPU-warp reasons changes bits and forces another golden bump. Pin them behind a versioned constant from day one.

Measured thread scaling on this container is only 2.0-2.4x on nproc=4 (shared/throttled cores), and the real passes are more memory-bound than the compute-heavy prototype — do not promise 4x; the stencil passes may land nearer 2x. The design's value is that the BITS are guaranteed at any thread count, so perf can be tuned freely later.

fs-simd's dot/sum are per-tier shapes: cross-ISA (NEON vs AVX2 vs scalar) bits differ within a documented envelope. Any accidental use of ops().sum/dot in a golden-bearing path silently breaks cross-machine bit-replay — needs a lint/review rule (elementwise ops only).
113 MB gather buffer at N=96 is fine but grows to ~905 MB at N=192; the slab-staged (wavefront) variant must be designed before the grid scales, or pass A/B fused per super-slab.

Hand-rolled std::thread::scope pool means gum-core owns panic containment and the workers=min(threads,tiles) rule itself (fs-exec's TilePool solved these but is unbuildable here); if asupersync ever lands, there will be two parallel-executor designs — keep the vendored reduce + pool with documented swap-back to fs-exec, mirroring the B3 jacobi_eigh de-vendoring that F3 already executed once.

The ANF arrest/accept controller is inherently serial and stateful (revert + velocity zero + dt shrink); parallelizing across iterations is impossible — speedup ceiling is entirely within one eval, so Amdahl leakage from the serial record/halo_fraction diagnostics (halo_fraction runs every record) should be checked before promising end-to-end numbers.

dimension: DIMENSION 3 — CPU→GPU design space for the gum-core kernels (fs-gum-field / fs-gum-statics)
findings: KERNEL SHAPES (from /home/user/fork_frankensim/analysis/gum-sandbox/gum-core/fs-gum-field/src/{field.rs,stencil.rs} and fs-gum-statics/src/engine.rs): the engine is five kernel families over a SoA flat Vec<f64>, component-major idx(a,ip,jp,kp)=((a*P+ip)*P+jp)*P+kp with P=N+4 (2-layer fixed-vacuum ghost rind). (1) POINTWISE sweeps: renormalize, tangent projection g-=(g.q)q, cell-density terms, ghost fill — embarrassingly parallel, fixed ascending (i,j,k) sweep order documented as the determinism contract. (2) STENCIL+ASSEMBLY forward pass: per eval point (N^3 cells for Central4 via derivs4's 13-point/axis-pair stencil c1=8/(12h), c2=1/(12h); (N+1)^3 corners for the Corner scheme's 8-cell nested averages) compute nn_dd dots + the 6-term det pair expansion (det_pairs, fixed PAIRS order), feeding 4 GLOBAL SCALAR REDUCTIONS (s_e2,s_e4,s_det,s_det2) plus a pointwise pass for s_e0,s_i — currently fixed-sequential-order sums. (3) GRADIENT pass: per-point flux P[3][4]+gq[4] (point_flux, ~500 flop/point incl. sextic cofactor) then a SCATTER to i±1,i±2 neighbors (Central4) or the 8 surrounding cells (Corner) with ghost-flux-dropped boundary conditions. (4) Grad::norm reduction. (5) Host-side control (arrested Newton flow, line search, guards) consumes only ~12 scalars per iteration — ideal for a device-resident field with tiny per-iteration readback.

THE ONE GPU-HOSTILE CONSTRUCT is the gradient scatter (engine.rs lines 366–460): atomics-free GPU execution requires rewriting it as a two-kernel gather — kernel A stores per-point (P[3][4],gq[4]) to an intermediate buffer (12 f64/point ≈ 85 MB at N=96, fine), kernel B has each REAL cell gather the adjoint-stencil contributions from the eval points that read it, in a fixed 13-term (Central4) or 8-term (Corner) order. This is translation-invariant so the gather stencil is just the transposed stencil with the same coefficients. Crucially the same gather formulation should be adopted by ALL backends (serial included) so CPU-serial, CPU-threaded and (aspirationally) GPU execute the identical add order per output cell — but this changes the serial engine's accumulation order and therefore its frozen bit-goldens: a versioned golden re-freeze (goldens-v2) on the new serial reference is an unavoidable program cost.

WGSL f64 STATUS (empirically nailed down in this container): the WGSL spec has no f64, but naga 30.0.0's WGSL frontend accepts an f64 extension ('f64' type, 'lf' literals); validation fails with Capabilities::empty() ('Type [0] is invalid') and passes with Capabilities::FLOAT64, which maps to wgpu Features::SHADER_F64 — a native-only feature backed by Vulkan shaderFloat64 (and partially DX12); Metal has no doubles, so the f64 path forfeits macOS/browser portability. SPIR-V GLSL.std.450 covers f64 sqrt (all the engine kernels need beyond +,-,*,/); f64 trig is NOT available but trig only appears in host-side seeding (sample_hedgehog uses fs_math::det trig on CPU), so kernels are clean.

HEADLESS VALIDATION IN THIS CONTAINER — three tiers all proven working: (a) cargo fetches new deps through the proxy fine (naga 30.0.0, wgpu 30.0.0, pollster all resolved and built from crates.io); (b) naga as a plain crate parses AND validates engine-shaped WGSL (a derivs4 compute shader) with zero GPU — this is the cheap always-on CI gate; (c) FULL EXECUTION: the container initially had NO Vulkan ICD (/etc/vulkan/icd.d empty, no /usr/share/vulkan, no EGL), but 'apt-get update && apt-get install mesa-vulkan-drivers' (25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.2, allowed by the proxy) installs lavapipe; wgpu 30 then enumerates 'llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2, 256 bits)' as a Vulkan CPU adapter with SHADER_F64=true, and a real f64 4th-order-stencil compute dispatch ran headlessly and came back BIT-IDENTICAL to the CPU f64 reference (max ulp diff 0, n=64). So the wgpu-f64 backend is exercisable end-to-end in CI in this very container.

RUST GPU OPTION SURVEY: wgpu/WGSL — actively maintained, one API over Vulkan/DX12/Metal/GL, f64 via SHADER_F64 (Vulkan-class devices + lavapipe), validated here; buffer ceilings: default max_storage_buffer_binding_size=128 MiB, max_buffer_size=256 MiB (wgpu-types-30.0.0/src/limits.rs:441-443) — a 4-component f64 field at N=192 is 241 MB, so either raise limits at device request (adapter-dependent) or exploit the component-major SoA layout to bind 4 per-component buffers (natural, zero-copy relayout). cust/CUDA (cudarc is the better-maintained 2025-era choice) — native f64 at full datacenter throughput, NVIDIA-only, requires nvcc/driver, CANNOT be validated in this container (no libcuda, no device) — keep as an optional later backend behind the same trait. rust-gpu — Rust→SPIR-V with Float64 capability exists but pins nightly toolchains and is ecosystem-risky for a certification program. OpenCL via ocl — cl_khr_fp64 is broadly available but the crate ecosystem is stagnant and no CL runtime is installed here. f32 alternatives (compensated summation, split-double/double-float) are NOT acceptable for the certified path: the program's gates sit at 1e-8..1e-13 class (E0/I 1e-8-class, FD-gradient 1.2e-6, clock ratio digits), f32 eps ~1.2e-7 destroys them, and double-float costs 15–20x flops with f32 exponent range; since f64-in-WGSL is empirically working, the fallback question is answered: STAY f64 END-TO-END.

DETERMINISM/CERTIFICATION MACHINERY ALREADY IN THE REPO: fs-flagship-e2e (crates/fs-flagship-e2e/src/lib.rs) defines the metric-golden pattern — a named metric stream folded into a content hash over IEEE-754 bit patterns (content_hash via fs_obs IdentityBuilder), wall time logged but excluded from the golden body, METRIC_STREAM_ENCODING_VERSION as a registered semantic surface, and the CONTRACT.md rule that stochastic/long stages must use metric-level (not bit-level) goldens. fs-ivl (crates/fs-ivl) provides outward-rounded Interval/Affine enclosures, cross-ISA bit-deterministic by construction — the certified-band primitive. These two compose directly into the two-tier GPU certificate described in the recommendation.

MEASURED SERIAL COST (scratch bench, path-deps on the real crates, release, this 4-core container): Central4 N=96 forward 54 ms / forward+grad 268 ms; Corner N=96 510 ms fwd+grad. Arrested Newton relaxation is thousands of grad evals, so an N=96 relax is ~10–45 min serial and N=192 (~8x/eval) is hours — this, not the N=48 gate suite, is what scaling buys. A deterministic 4-core threaded backend (static k-slab partition, fixed reduction tree) should give ~3.5x immediately; a modest f64 GPU another ~5–20x on the compute-heavy gradient pass (consumer GeForce f64 ALU is 1:64 so gains are bandwidth-side; datacenter 1:2 f64 gets the full win).
design_recommendation: Build a new sandbox crate `fs-gum-kernels` (same out-of-workspace pattern — the fork's workspace root still does not resolve, per PORTABILITY.md) that (1) reifies the kernel SPEC as data — stencil coefficient tables, the PAIRS det expansion, the adjoint (gather-form) stencil, and a FIXED-TOPOLOGY pairwise reduction tree keyed only to N (never to thread count) — and (2) defines a `Backend` trait: upload/download(Field3), fill_ghosts, forward_sums(&Opts)->SectorSums, flux_pass (point → P/gq intermediate buffer), adjoint_gather, cell_terms_and_project, renormalize, reduce_scalar/reduce_norm. Three impls: (a) `serial` — the reference, rewritten scatter→gather with the fixed reduction tree; it re-derives the goldens (versioned goldens-v2, since the add order changes; gate the new serial against the old engine at machine-eps-class tolerance once, then re-freeze bit-goldens); (b) `threaded` — std::thread scoped, static slab decomposition, per-chunk partials combined in fixed chunk order using the identical tree, hence BIT-IDENTICAL to serial by construction (assert hash equality in CI on this 4-core box); (c) `wgpu` — f64 WGSL kernels (SHADER_F64 / naga Capabilities::FLOAT64), one compute pipeline per kernel, field resident on device, ~12 scalars read back per Newton iteration; 4 per-component storage buffers to stay under the 128 MiB binding default up to N≥256. The f64 question is answered concretely: f64 end-to-end via the wgpu/naga extension — proven working headlessly on lavapipe in this container — with NO f32/compensated fallback on the certified path; an optional cudarc/CUDA backend behind the same trait is deferred until a datacenter-class f64 GPU is the real target. CI validation ladder (all runnable here): tier 1 naga parse+validate of every WGSL kernel as a unit test (no GPU, milliseconds); tier 2 full wgpu execution on lavapipe (mesa-vulkan-drivers) with the complete gate suite; tier 3 real-GPU runs certified by the two-tier certificate. CERTIFICATION, precisely: adopt the fs-flagship-e2e metric-golden pattern — a fixed-order named metric stream (e2,e4,e6,e0,I,deg,estat,floor_gap,grad_norm at declared checkpoints + final relaxed values + iteration count) hashed over IEEE-754 bits. Tier A (CPU backends): the metric-stream hash MUST equal the frozen golden hash — bit-identical, exactly the v3 discipline. Tier B (GPU): at golden-freeze time the serial reference also emits, per metric, a certified fs-ivl Interval enclosure (forward pass replayed once in interval arithmetic — the enclosure is the tolerance band, not a hand-tuned epsilon); a GPU run is CERTIFIED iff (i) every emitted metric lies inside its frozen enclosure (fs-checker adjudicates), (ii) the run reproduces ITS OWN metric bits under replay on the same adapter+driver (per-device bit-replay is demanded even when cross-device identity is not), and (iii) the evidence record binds adapter name, driver info, and pipeline/shader hashes so any future delta is attributable. Bit-agreement of lavapipe with serial (observed here: exact) is recorded as informative evidence, never required — real drivers may FMA-contract.

GPU f64 throughput context (knowledge, not measured — no real GPU here): consumer GeForce f64:f32 ALU ratio 1:64 (Ampere/Ada), datacenter A100/H100 1:2; forward stencil pass is bandwidth-bound (~0.9 flop/byte) so consumer cards still win there; the ~500-flop/point sextic gradient is where 1:64 bites
risks: Golden re-freeze is forced: the scatter→gather adjoint rewrite changes the serial add order, so every fs-gum-statics/e2e bit-golden that touches gradients must be re-derived (goldens-v2 with a one-time machine-eps-class equivalence gate against the old engine) — a discipline cost the program must budget explicitly, and the highest-leverage thing to get right first

wgpu f64 is a native-only extension, not WebGPU: no Metal (macOS dev machines) and no browser; the portable-f64 surface is effectively Vulkan (+lavapipe) — if Mac-local execution ever matters, only the CPU backends run there

Cross-device bit-identity is NOT promised even with strict naga output: driver shader compilers may FMA-contract or reassociate; the design's per-device replay + fs-ivl band certificate absorbs this, but a device whose driver upgrade shifts bits will need its evidence record re-frozen (attributable, by design, via the bound driver/pipeline hashes)

lavapipe CI green ≠ device certified: llvmpipe executes f64 as strict LLVM scalar code (hence the observed bit-identity); a real GPU is the first place tier-B certification is actually exercised, and no real GPU exists in this container — the wgpu backend ships CI-validated but hardware-uncertified until someone runs it on metal

Consumer-GPU f64 gradient throughput may disappoint (1:64 ALU): if the target hardware is GeForce-class, the compute-heavy sextic cofactor pass may only reach ~2-5x over the 4-core threaded backend; the CUDA/cudarc option or datacenter parts fix this but were explicitly not validatable here

apt-installed mesa-vulkan-drivers is container-state, not repo-state: CI recipes must install it explicitly (documented apt-get update first — the direct install 404s on stale indexes); if the proxy policy ever blocks archive.ubuntu.com, tier-2 CI degrades to naga-only static validation

fs-ivl interval replay of the forward pass at N=96 is a one-time but nontrivial cost (intervals ~4-8x scalar cost, so ~minutes per golden freeze) and interval blowup on the sextic det terms could make bands loose; fallback is the Higham-style a-priori gamma_n bound on the fixed-shape sums, which is coarser but still rigorous

wgpu API churn is real (this survey hit 6 breaking API differences between wgpu ~25-era knowledge and wgpu 30: async enumerate_adapters, InstanceDescriptor construction, PollType::wait_indefinitely, Result-returning get_mapped_range, etc.) — pin the wgpu/naga major version in the crate and treat upgrades as certified-surface changes

The new crates must stay in the out-of-workspace sandbox pattern (empty [workspace], path deps): the fork's workspace root still fails to resolve (fs-exec → absent ../asupersync sibling, PORTABILITY.md), so any temptation to put fs-gum-kernels in crates/ hits the same wall

dimension: DIMENSION 1 — Measured CPU performance profile of the gum-core crates (4-core Cascade Lake-class Xeon @ 2.8 GHz fixed, AVX-512 present, L1d 32 KiB/core, L2 1 MiB/core, L3 33 MiB shared, 15 GB RAM)
findings: Every gum-core binary is strictly single-threaded today: all three gate runs show user == real (field 1.96s/2.12s, statics 298.4s/299.0s, e2e 206.1s/206.3s). The 4 cores are 75% idle during a 5-minute gate suite.

The hot loop is fs-gum-statics/src/engine.rs::eval(): per ANF iteration it makes TWO full for_each_point sweeps (forward pass, then gradient pass that RECOMPUTES the same stencil derivatives), each sweep doing per-point: stencil read (24 neighbor loads central4 / 32 loads corner), nn_dd quaternion dot products, the 6-term PAIRS determinant expansion, point_flux (the (2+4) flux + sextic cofactor), then a 13-point adjoint SCATTER (central4) or 8-cell signed scatter (corner) into the Grad array. anf.rs adds renormalize() plus ~6 vector sweeps over 4N^3 (v update, q step via get/set, save_cells, tangent re-projection, g.norm()) — measured at <6% of iteration cost. Decomposed ANF iteration at N=96: eval-grad 0.502 s + renorm 0.006 s + vector ops ~0.020 s = 0.528 s; the bench's N=48 composite (0.067 s/iter) matches the gates' measured 69.8-71.3 ms/iter, validating the model.

The kernels are COMPUTE-BOUND by a ~20x margin, and specifically SCALAR-ISSUE-bound, not SIMD-peak-bound: hand-counted ~700 FLOPs/point for central4 grad-eval and ~1090 FLOPs/corner-point for the corner descent path give achieved 1.9-3.1 GFLOP/s = 0.7-1.1 FLOPs/cycle, versus a measured 11.3 GFLOP/s SSE2 vector peak (mul-add loop) and ~90 GFLOP/s theoretical AVX-512 FMA peak per core. DRAM demand during descent is ~0.3-0.5 GB/s against 11.7 GB/s measured single-thread STREAM triad (23.5 GB/s 4-thread aggregate). Arithmetic intensity ~5 FLOP/byte of unique traffic.

Cache behavior is benign even at N=192: the stencil's 5-plane reuse window (5 planes x 4 components x 196^2 x 8 B = 6.1 MB) fits the 33 MB L3, so corner grad-eval degrades only 553 -> 622 ns/pt (+13%) from N=48 to N=192 despite the field alone being 241 MB. Central4 grad degrades 223 -> 324 ns/pt (+45%), stabilizing by N=128.

SURPRISE, load-bearing for the scaling design: rebuilding with -C target-cpu=native (AVX-512) makes the real kernels 10-25% SLOWER (corner grad N=192: 4.47 -> 5.21 s; central4 grad N=96: 277 -> 338 ns/pt) while the synthetic FMA loop speeds up 11.3 -> 19.1 GFLOP/s. The per-point [f64;4] local-array style defeats the autovectorizer; compiler flags are a dead end — the speedup must come from restructured k-contiguous sweep kernels and threading. (Printed physics checksums were identical between baseline and native builds — Rust's no-FP-contraction default held.)

Multiprocess scaling is essentially perfect: 4 concurrent copies of gum_field_gates finish in 1.824 s vs 1.804 s for one — 3.96x throughput. With bandwidth 20x under-subscribed, domain-decomposed threading of the point sweeps should scale near-linearly to 4 cores at every N measured.

Two determinism hazards block naive parallelization of exactly these loops: (a) all reductions (s_e2/s_e4/s_det/s_det2, g.norm, renormalize drift-max) are fixed-order sequential sums — any thread-count-dependent reduction order breaks bit-identity; (b) the gradient is written as an adjoint SCATTER (read-modify-write of up to 13 cells per point), a data race under threads. Both have deterministic fixes: per-slab (not per-thread) partial sums combined in fixed slab order, and inverting scatter to gather. (c) ANF itself is globally sequential — accept/reject and the dt arrest cascade branch on the exact objective value, so a 1-ulp difference can flip an arrest and diverge the whole trajectory; cross-backend goldens must therefore be endpoint tolerance-band/metric goldens (the v2 assessment's sanctioned fallback), with bit-identity reserved for same-backend replay.

Per-stage timing of gum_statics_gates run 1 (~149 s; suite doubles it for replay): radial solve N=4000 0.1 s; G-A FD-vs-analytic gradient gate N=24 0.6 s; G-B static ANF N=48 x 900 iters 62.8 s; G-C main descent 600 iters 42.8 s; G-C control 600 iters 42.2 s; G-D clock bisection <1 s. The three ANF descents are 99% of the suite — the descent loop is the ONLY thing worth parallelizing. Same shape in e2e: relax 900 iters 62.1 s + isorotation 600 iters 40.6 s = 99.6% of its 103 s run-1; the topo/Hopf stages are 0.4 s.
design_recommendation: Build the kernel architecture around ONE parallel primitive: a domain-decomposed 'sweep' over evaluation points that fuses (stencil-read -> per-point physics -> per-point flux) and returns (a) per-slab partial reductions and (b) per-point flux/density records consumed by a GATHER-formulated adjoint (each cell gathers the 13/8 contributions that today are scattered to it). This single restructuring simultaneously: removes the RMW race, makes the k-inner loop vectorizable (SoA layout already has k contiguous), and makes reductions bit-identical for ANY thread count by fixing the partial-sum topology to slabs (sum slab partials in fixed slab order) — preserving the determinism discipline on CPU 1T, CPU 4T, and CI. Keep the existing serial code as the golden referee. For GPU, the same sweep+gather maps directly to one thread per point; at AI ≈ 5 FLOP/B the kernel sits near the memory roofline of an A100-class part (~1.5 TB/s -> ~7 TFLOP/s effective, ~3000x this box's measured 1.9-2.5 GFLOP/s serial), so goldens there must be the tolerance-band/metric kind at descent ENDPOINTS (deg, Estat, kappa, halo within bands), never per-iteration bit compares — the ANF arrest cascade amplifies 1-ulp differences into divergent trajectories. Do NOT rely on compiler flags: measured target-cpu=native is a 10-25% regression on the real kernels; explicit restructuring (plane-blocked sweeps, optionally cached derivatives to kill the double stencil evaluation, +12N^3 doubles = 85 MB at N=192, affordable in 15 GB) is where the ~4x SIMD x 3.96x thread headroom (~15x single-box) actually lives. CPU-only feasibility on this 4-core box: every roadmap target below is minutes-to-under-an-hour at 4 threads, so the CPU tier of the architecture is viable without GPU.

risks: Bit-identity vs parallelism: every reduction in sector.rs/engine.rs/anf.rs is a fixed-order sequential f64 sum (an explicit contract in the code comments). Naive rayon/atomic reductions break golden roots. Mitigation exists (fixed per-slab partials independent of thread count) but must be designed in from kernel one, and cross-backend (CPU vs GPU) bit-identity for full descents should be declared out of scope up front: the ANF arrest cascade (obj > obj_prev branch, dt *= 0.6) turns 1-ulp objective differences into macroscopically different trajectories — endpoint tolerance-band/metric goldens are the correct target, per the v2 assessment's stated fallback.

The gradient's adjoint-scatter (13 RMW targets per point central4, 8 per corner) is a data race under any threading; the gather rewrite changes floating-point ACCUMULATION ORDER into g, so even the deterministic fix changes goldens once — plan a one-time golden re-freeze (or an order-preserving gather) and gate the rewrite with the existing G-A FD-vs-analytic check (1e-5) plus X-gate forward consistency (1e-12).

target-cpu=native measured as a 10-25% kernel regression: any assumption that GPUs or wider SIMD give 'free' speedup proportional to peak FLOPs is falsified on this code shape; per-kernel measurement gates are needed at every backend step.

Projections for N=128/N=192 assume iteration counts (3000, 2100) and unchanged arrest behavior at higher resolution; arrests/dt dynamics at N>96 are unmeasured — actual counts could differ by 2x either way. Also per-iteration cost was measured on the hedgehog field; halo-spread endpoints have the same FLOP count (dense sweeps), so this risk is confined to iteration counts, not s/iter.

No GPU exists in this container: all GPU numbers here are roofline extrapolations from measured AI (~5 FLOP/B), not measurements; the 4T numbers are extrapolated from 4-process scaling of an N<=96 workload — at N=192 four threads share one field but the 6.1 MB/thread L3 reuse window x4 = 24.4 MB approaches the 33 MB L3, so 4T efficiency at N=192 could dip below 3.96x (unmeasured).
Fixed 2.8 GHz under KVM hypervisor: no turbo observed, but co-tenancy noise on shared hosts can perturb wall-clock gates; the 300 s statics suite already varies 296-299 s run to run.

dimension: DIMENSION 4 — Physics demand survey: which GUM computations actually need scale
findings: I.2 3D two-knot gradient flow (the bond-equation closed loop, releases r1+r6): NEVER EXECUTED in this repo — grep confirms no two-knot/orientation relaxation code exists anywhere under analysis/gum-sandbox; only the pair-law ARITHMETIC was checked (F-R8, REPLICATION_CAMPAIGN_STATUS.md line 227). The protocol (paper App I.2, line 714 of 01-GUM-Omega-Paper-v2.0.1.md): three orientations (pi/perpendicular/spin-axis channels per Thm VII.2), a separation scan over the mandatory calibration window x in [1.5,3] (App H, line 710), a B_eff estimator fit, closing the loop x0 = 1.90+/-0.05 predicted from b=42 vs 1.92+/-0.08 measured; stretch target the r6 clock-coherent locked bond x0_lock = 2.42+/-0.12 via the cos(dPhi) transverse channel. Box: two knots at d = x*R* up to 3R* = 5.35 with Yukawa tails at mu = 1/sqrt(2t) = 7.77 (t = 0.008276434949296802) needing only ~1.78 units of margin for 1e-6 tail truncation — a 144x96x96 grid at the certified h = 0.09375 (1.33M cells, exactly 1.5x the certified single-knot 96^3). The kernel needed (arrested Newton flow with analytic gradients, guards, sector energies) EXISTS and is certified in fs-gum-statics (18/18 gates) — I.2 is a new driver + seeding (symmetrized product ansatz) + estimator on top of an existing kernel, not new physics code.

I.2 cost is threaded-CPU class: extrapolating the measured fs-gum-statics rate (~0.59 us/cell/iter single-core, from ~150 s per gate-suite pass dominated by 2100 ANF iters at N=48), the two-knot grid runs ~0.78 s/iter single-core, ~0.24 s/iter on 4 threads; a full campaign of ~24 relaxations (3 orientations x ~8 separations) x ~1500 ANF iters (campaign ANF experience 600-3000: statics used 900+600+600 at caps, Python field3d used 1200) is ~2.4 h on 4 threads, ~1e14 FLOP total. Memory ~200-300 MB. It is also the ideal kernel-architecture exercise: an embarrassingly parallel outer task farm (24 independent relaxations -> 4-core saturation with per-run bit-identical goldens preserved) plus a domain-decomposable inner stencil kernel (the GPU-portable layer), and its headline outputs (x0, B_eff, channel coefficients) are exactly the tolerance-band/metric-golden kind the v2 assessment sanctions when bit-identity breaks under threading.

F-R5 N=192 halo-endpoint refinement: feasible on 4 threaded cores. 192^3 = 7.08M cells (8x the N=96 referee), field 226 MB, ANF state ~0.9 GB. At the measured rate: ~4.2 s/iter single-core, ~1.3 s/iter on 4 threads; a static-relax + over-spun-main + control triple at ~2000 iters each (~6000 iters) is ~2.2 h, ~0.85e14 FLOP. Reference points: Python field3d N=96 full suite took 4461 s on 4 cores (field3d_RESULTS.md line 270); Rust N=48 suite ~5 min including double replay. Scientific value: directly hardens the DISCHARGE_PACKAGE's F-R5 claim (halo endpoint, kappa -> 1/sqrt(2) saturation) with a convergence rung the corpus's authors cannot dismiss as lattice artifact — but it refines a number the campaign already owns rather than replicating something untouched.

Saturated-closure G* vs c0 at high precision: CPU-TRIVIAL and the highest science-per-FLOP item on the board. DISCHARGE_PACKAGE/README.md lines 250-254: G* converges downward with basis size to 2.51442-2.51446 (two independent engines agree at 6e-5), within ~1.2e-4 of c0 = 2.514735 and still decreasing — 'whether they coincide in some limit is open'. The instrument is the tier2 axi3/axi4 2-D spectral engine (N=720 basis, gradient residuals ~1e-6, internal identity E_core + E0_halo = (3/2)G* at 2.2e-16). A basis-enrichment + Richardson-extrapolation push (possibly extended precision) is <=1e12 FLOP, sub-hour on ONE core. If G* = c0 exactly, that is a new exact identity in the corpus's flagship constant; if not, the gap becomes a quantitative finding. Too cheap to be a scale demo — run it as the free companion result in the same release.

I.6 3D T-KILL (2e-5) and D3 (8e-4, depth 5) SPLIT by precision: these are trajectory-ensemble statistics on conditional wavefunctions (Prop VIII.2 / Thm VIII.1, paper line 572). The B4 fs-gum-sde machinery (Philox WienerStream, mode-sum psi, osmotic velocity) is the right kernel; measured throughput 20,000 trajectories x ~6283 steps in ~320 s (vs born.py 829 s). D3-grade 8e-4 needs ~(sigma/8e-4)^2 ~ 4e5 trajectories — hours on 4 cores, CPU-FEASIBLE. T-KILL-grade 2e-5 on a coincidence null needs ~(sigma/2e-5)^2 ~ 6e8 trajectories in 3D: ~3e7 core-seconds ~ 3 months on 4 cores — GPU-NEEDED via the trajectory-parallel route (embarrassingly parallel, counter-based RNG already gives order-independent draws — the ONE GUM workload whose determinism contract survives GPU reduction trivially). Caveat: a deterministic conditional-wavefunction quadrature could cut this by orders of magnitude; the demand estimate assumes the MC route.

I.7 tower-depth area-law study ('area-law: 3-5, N-independent to 12', paper line 714): a configuration-space/mode-tower entanglement study at small N (to 12) — exact-diagonalization/mode-sum class, CPU-cheap-to-moderate (<=1e12 FLOP), no scale story. Low priority for the scale program.

II.H blue-fog chiral condensate box (disclination-web ground state, Thm H-3, paper lines 123-131): GENUINELY GPU-CLASS, confirming the roadmap's own 'blue-fog GPU boxes — out of envelope' classification (ROADMAP_v3.md line 74). What it needs: soft-sector director/quaternion field with chiral term at 'm' = 1.9 +/- 0.4 near threshold, a box of >=10-20 pitch lengths per side with disclination cores resolved (>=16-32 cells/pitch) -> 256^3 minimum, 512^3 credible; glassy double-twist-network annealing needs 1e5-1e6 sweeps and an ensemble of ~5-10 quenches to demonstrate 'locally helical, globally statistically isotropic' (F8/F13). FLOP: ~2.5e16 (256^3 pilot) to ~4e17 (512^3 study) — 1 week to 1.3 years on 4 CPU cores vs hours-to-a-day on one A100/H100-class GPU. Diagnostics needed already exist in fs-gum-topo (Z/2 disclination loop holonomy, defect-line tracing, Hopf) — the missing piece is scale, making this the honest GPU-rung target. Payoffs staked on it: the phason stiffness f window, sin(theta_c) = 0.69 +/- 0.11, and the F-hel isotropy discharge.

Determinism discipline across the ladder: fs-gum-statics's contract is explicitly 'plain sequential f64 loops in fixed ascending (point,component) order — no tree reductions, no parallelism' (RESULTS.md Determinism statement). Threading therefore breaks bit-identity ONLY at reductions; stencil/gradient scatter is per-cell independent. A fixed-tile decomposition with per-tile sequential reduction and a fixed-order tile combine keeps bit-identical goldens on the CPU rung at fixed thread-tile geometry; GPU rungs fall to the v2 assessment's sanctioned fallback (tolerance-band/metric goldens), which the I.2 observables (fitted x0, B_eff) are naturally shaped for.
design_recommendation: Flagship for the threaded-CPU rung: the I.2 two-knot bond-equation closed loop — the prior is CONFIRMED and strengthened by inspection. It is the only App-I protocol that (a) has never been executed anywhere in this repo (grep-verified: no two-knot relaxation code exists; the campaign only checked the pair-law arithmetic), (b) reuses the certified fs-gum-statics ANF kernel unchanged on a grid just 1.5x the certified single-knot referee (144x96x96 at the frozen h=0.09375), (c) fits the 4-core budget with margin (~2.4 h for the full 3-orientation x 8-separation campaign, ~1e14 FLOP, ~300 MB), (d) exercises BOTH parallelism levels the kernel architecture must prove — an outer task farm over 24 independent relaxations (perfect 4-core scaling with per-run bit-identity intact) and an inner domain-decomposable stencil kernel that is the GPU-portable object, and (e) delivers a headline closed-loop science number (x0 = 1.90+/-0.05 predicted from b=42 vs the corpus's 1.92+/-0.08; stretch: the r6 locked bond 2.42+/-0.12) whose fitted-observable form is exactly the tolerance-band golden the determinism doctrine prescribes for the parallel rungs. Sequence the release as: (1) G* vs c0 high-precision 2-D spectral push FIRST — sub-hour, single-core, potentially a new exact identity, zero architecture risk; (2) I.2 two-knot flagship on the new threaded kernel; (3) N=192 F-R5 halo endpoint as the second workload proving the same kernel scales 8x in cells (hardens the DISCHARGE_PACKAGE). Genuinely GPU-needed and honestly deferred to the GPU rung: the II.H blue-fog disclination-web box (2.5e16-4e17 FLOP — the roadmap already classes it GPU) and T-KILL at the full 2e-5 (~6e8 3D Nelson trajectories, ~3e7 core-seconds; trajectory-parallel with Philox counter-based draws, so it is also the GPU workload with the cleanest determinism story). Do NOT build the scale program around I.7 or D3-grade I.6 — both are CPU-cheap and prove nothing about the architecture.

II.H blue-fog box: 256^3 x 1e5 sweeps x 5 quenches ~ 2.5e16 FLOP (pilot); 512^3 x 2e5 x 5 ~ 4e17 FLOP (study) at ~3 kflop/cell/sweep — ~1 week to ~1.3 years on 4 CPU cores at ~1e10 FLOP/s vs ~1-11 h on one ~1e13 FLOP/s GPU — estimated here; consistent with ROADMAP_v3 line 74's standing 'blue-fog GPU boxes' out-of-envelope classification

Certified baseline being scaled: fs-gum-statics 18/18 gates, N=48 relax + two descents + clock in ~150 s/pass, 75 gate f64s bit-identical across runs, BLAKE3 6b3959d4... (fs-gum-statics/RESULTS.md); single-knot referee N=96 central4 worst sector 2.7e-3, virial -6.6e-4 (field3d_RESULTS.md / gap_survey_v3.json)
risks: Timing extrapolations come from one measured point (N=48 gate suite, ~65 ms/iter inferred, not separately instrumented); stencil kernels are memory-bandwidth-bound, so N=144x96x96 and 192^3 could run 1.5-3x slower per cell than N=48 (cache working set 40x-64x larger) — budget headroom or instrument a per-iteration timer before committing wall-time claims.

ANF iteration counts at larger grids are uncertain: dt is capped at 0.05 with arrest-driven shrink; halved effective resolution or two-knot saddle geometry may force smaller dt and 2-3x more iterations (all three certified runs already ended at iter_cap, not convergence).

The I.2 protocol is one sentence in App I.2 — fit window, B_eff estimator, orientation definitions, and two-knot seeding (symmetrized product ansatz vs constrained separation) must be reconstructed; at small x the pair may relax toward a merged B=2 configuration, likely requiring a separation constraint/pinning mechanism fs-gum-statics does not yet have. The measured x0 could land outside the corpus band for protocol reasons rather than physics reasons — publish the estimator definition as part of the golden.

Threaded bit-identity is achievable only with fixed tile decomposition and fixed-order combines, and the golden is then tied to thread/tile geometry; cross-geometry runs need the tolerance-band fallback — state this in the determinism contract up front, or the '91 gates bit-replay' discipline will appear to regress.

T-KILL 2e-5 demand (~6e8 trajectories) assumes the Monte Carlo route with per-trajectory sigma ~ 0.5; a deterministic conditional-wavefunction quadrature or variance-reduction (the fs-rand Sobol machinery) could cut orders of magnitude — the GPU-needed classification for I.6 is route-dependent, unlike blue-fog which is grid-bound.

Blue-fog box numbers are the softest in the survey: pitch length in lattice units is a free modeling choice, near-threshold (m = 1.9) double-twist networks are glassy and may need far more than 1e5-2e5 sweeps to equilibrate, and no GPU exists in this container to validate any GPU throughput assumption — treat 2.5e16-4e17 FLOP as an order-of-magnitude envelope, not a plan.

The G* vs c0 push may be limited by f64 conditioning rather than basis size (current engines agree only at 6e-5); extended precision or a reformulated objective may be needed, which is new numerics, not just a bigger run.

All feasibility classes assume the fs-gum-statics functional as-is; the two-knot runs put weight on the guard machinery (degree anchor, Bogomolny wall) in a two-charge sector where the frozen guard parameters were never calibrated — guard-induced artifacts in the bond energy are a within-model validity risk.
